speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Merchant Shipping (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act was passed last year, to implement the Salvage Convention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A key aspect of the Salvage Convention is the introduction of special compensation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: These are compensation for claims arising from salvage operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Special compensation claims allow a salvor to be compensated for salvage operations to prevent or minimise environmental damage, even if the salvor did not save the vessel or its cargo.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Currently, the High Court's admiralty jurisdiction covers only traditional salvage claims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: I will highlight the key amendments very quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 2 amends the current section 3(1)(i) of the Act, which relates to salvage claims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 2 provides that the High Court's admiralty jurisdiction includes any claim arising under the Salvage Convention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes Article 14 of the Salvage Convention, which provides for special compensation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: It also provides that the High Court's admiralty jurisdiction covers contractual claims relating to salvage services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This includes contractual clauses that provide for special compensation, such as the Special Compensation Protection and Indemnity clause.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This ensures that all salvage claims previously covered by admiralty jurisdiction continue to be covered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 2 also preserves the principle that there is parity in treatment of claims arising from salvage operations in respect of both ships and aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Clause 3 of the Bill repeals section 176 of the Merchant Shipping Act, which provides that the High Court has jurisdiction to decide all claims relating to salvage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This provision is a historical anachronism and is unnecessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The High Court (Admiralty Jurisdiction) Act already provides for admiralty jurisdiction over salvage-related claims and it should be the single piece of legislation dealing with this issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Situated in a strategic geographical location with strong supporting networks comprising professional services, marine technology and logistical solutions, Singapore was ranked as the leading maritime capital of the world in 2019.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Singapore has taken active steps to accede to the International Convention on Salvage.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While that Act paved the way for the substantive law, it is this Bill deals with the jurisdiction of the High Court with respect to salvage claims.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Salvage operation refers to any act or activity undertaken to assist a vessel or any other property in danger in navigable waters or in any other waters whatsoever.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The party doing the salvage operation is known as a salvor.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Situations that give rise to the need for salvage are varied, for example, grounding, fire, collisions, engine failure, structural failure and sinking.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Previously, the 1910 Brussels Convention for the Unification of Certain Rules of Law respecting Assistance and Salvage at Sea, salvors would only be rewarded if they were successful.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, this did not adequately recognise the skills and efforts of salvors who prevented or minimised environmental damage, providing little incentive for riskier salvage operations.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: An example is where a major pollution incident was avoided by towing a damaged tanker away from an environmentally sensitive area of where the ship or cargo could not be salvaged.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In light of this, the 1989 International Convention on Salvage introduced something called "special compensation".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This provided some reward to salvors who prevented or minimised environmental damage even though they were unsuccessful in saving the ship or the cargo.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, this law is important and I support it because it will further incentivise and encourage ships at sea to help fellow ships in distress to reduce environmental damage within the seas and oceans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Reduction of environmental damage to the seas and oceans are key and we should support such a reduction.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill has two operative clauses – clauses 2 and 3.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The way the relevant provision has been restructured sets out more clearly what is covered.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Flowing from this restructuring though, would the Minister please clarify if there is any other difference in the admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court over salvage claims besides the addition of salvage claims under the Convention?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By allowing special compensation claims in the Singapore High Court, our High Court will have an expanded jurisdiction over a variety of claims in admiralty law and places it in a good position to administer justice on admiralty claims.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This furthers Singapore's position as a dispute resolution hub, particularly in the admiralty law practice.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the press release on MinLaw's website on this Bill dated 4 May 2020, paragraph 3 states and I quote, "By placing special compensation claims on the same footing as traditional salvage claims, the Bill incentivises salvors to protect the environment during salvage operations".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister please clarify whether the statement that special compensation claims are placed on the same footing as traditional salvage claims is to be understood only in the context of High Court admiralty jurisdiction and not, for instance, the ranking of a maritime lien?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Minister please also elaborate how having a High Court jurisdiction over special compensation claims impacts salvors and incentivises them to protect the environment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Further, would the Minister be able to explain whether the introduction of special compensation might translate into a better marine environment near Singapore shores?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Clause 3 repeals section 176 of the Merchant Shipping Act which provides for the jurisdiction of the High Court over salvage claims in addition to section 3(1)(i) of the High Court (Admiralty Jurisdiction) Act.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By locating all relevant provisions under the same Act, clause 3 tidies our statute book and makes the law clearer.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: That Convention more adequately reflects the service that salvors do and incentivises salvors to protect the environment.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill furthers and strengthens Singapore as a maritime dispute resolution hub and a key maritime capital in the world and, therefore, I support this Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The High Court (Admiralty Jurisdiction) Act sets out the Admiralty jurisdiction of our High Court.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A robust admiralty law and regime is always important to a major international maritime hub.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singapore is one of the major maritime hubs in the world alongside Hong Kong and London.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One other advantage we have had for many years is that we have one of the busiest ports in the world and many ships stop by for bunkering, transhipment or other services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many ships also passed by Singapore en route to ports elsewhere in the world.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A busy port allows greater possibility of seizing jurisdiction for admiralty claims in our courts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Merchant Shipping (Miscellaneous Amendment) Act brought into force two key maritime conventions, one of which is the International Convention on Salvage of 1989.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Today, the proposed amendments to the High Court (Admiralty Jurisdiction) Act (HCAJA) are consequential to the adoption of the Salvage Convention in our laws.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The HCAJA provides for the admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It essentially sets out the various maritime claims allowed under our admiralty law and how admiralty jurisdiction can be invoked for any claim and against any ship or any company or even individual.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It also provides that services rendered in saving life from a ship is made under the Salvage Convention and not under a previous provision.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I said we could address this issue in our law by including an extended definition of "damage to the environment" to any place where the damage may occur and the "fair rate" as referred to in Article 14 is deemed to include an element of profit, just like what South Africa did in their law.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: More importantly, they encourage salvors to carry out salvage work on a vessel which by itself or its cargo threatened damage to environment or to prevent or minimise damage to environment even when the salvage work did not result in the ship or cargo being salved.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In this way, salvors will not be motivated solely by or pressured merely by the need to achieve a positive salvage in terms of the ship or cargo.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This will encourage salvors to place significant consideration on possible damage to environment or to mitigate such damage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is consistent with environmental concerns of the international community which developed in the last 30 years as a result of the huge damage to environment caused by numerous notorious cases like the Exxon Valdez, the Erika, the MSC Prestige and which also led to changes in the United Nations Convention on Law of the Sea and the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza asks if the Bill change the High Court's admiralty jurisdiction over salvage claims, other than adding claims currently proposed under the Salvage Convention.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But in other respects, the jurisdiction of the High Court is preserved.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza also asked about ranking and whether the Bill provides for special compensation claims to enjoy a maritime lien.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Bill does not do so and let me explain this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Today, the common law grants traditional salvage claims a maritime lien because property has been saved, either the vessel itself or the cargo.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And this in turn ensures that there are assets from which all other claims can then be paid.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This rationale, however, does not apply or may not apply to special compensation claims, because these claims arise in situations where possibly, neither the vessel nor the cargo has been saved.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also considered international practice on whether these claims are given a ranking of a maritime lien.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Jurisdictions like the UK and Hong Kong, who have similarly expanded their admiralty jurisdiction laws to cover special compensation claims, have not provided legislatively for such claims to be conferred a maritime lien.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The 1993 International Convention on Maritime Liens and Mortgages, which 19 countries have acceded to, also does not provide for special compensation claims to give rise to maritime liens.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For these reasons, the Bill does not confer a lien on such claims.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Both Mr de Souza and Mr Tan touched on the impact that this Bill has on the environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza asked, in particular, how this Bill might incentivise salvors in the context of environmental protection.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Today, salvors commonly obtain security to satisfy their special compensation claims through the relevant P&I clubs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This Bill provides an additional avenue for obtaining security for such claims.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This avenue may be needed where contractual arrangements for security are absent, or could perhaps, in some cases, be inadequate.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: By broadening the range of enforcement options available, this amendment gives salvors greater assurance of compensation when they undertake operations to protect the environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza asked how the introduction of such claims might affect the eco-system of such projects and the environment near Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The mechanism of special compensation was created to ensure that salvors are incentivised to assist endangered vessels that might provide a threat to the environment.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr de Souza might be aware that under the Salvage Convention, salvors who engage in salvage operations in any waters will be able to enforce special compensation claims in any proceedings brought before a Court or arbitral tribunal in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the availability of such claims under our current framework will be a positive development for the marine environment, generally, and also for Singapore.
